source: Open Archieven (openarchieven.nl), the open API of Coret Genealogie
licence: Open data — Open Archieven publishes its data openly and asks that the HOLDING ARCHIVE be named as the source, which every row here does in its title; no more than four requests a second, and a recognisable program name, both observed.
note: One claim per archive, carrying the places it holds records for and the archive's own record count for each. THESE ARE INDEX ENTRIES, NOT SCANS: a record is a name, a date and a shelf reference, and whether an image exists is the holding archive's business. THE PLACE LIST IS TRUNCATED FOR THE LARGEST ARCHIVES: the API stops reporting distinct places at 200, which 107 of 193 archives reach — the Brabants Historisch Informatie Centrum covers the whole of North Brabant and is given 200. (Some of those show 199 here because one of the 200 was a blank place name, which this harvest drops.) The other 86 are listed in full. A truncated archive is represented by the places it holds the MOST records for, so a dot that misses out is one it barely touches. `records` is the archive's own total and is NOT the sum of the places shown.
